mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the general partner's home jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (under Hague Convention of 5 October 1961) for Convention parties; otherwise consular legalization by the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed lawyer or notary in the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Canadian consular legalization, as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against: (i) Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c 17), the United Nations Act (R.S.C. 1985, c U-2), and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (S.C. 2011, c 21); (ii) the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) consolidated sanctions list; (iii) the OFAC SDN list for all USD-denominated transactions; and (iv) the domestic PEP records maintained through FINTRAC. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs and non-resident partners, with risk-based ongoing monitoring for a minimum term of 12 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — secure online filing and name clearance portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every proposed name must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The legal name of a limited partnership must be in French and must include the designating terms 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; trademarks and proper nouns may remain in their original form, but generic English tokens (e.g., 'Global', 'Trade') require a French equivalent unless an authorization is obtained from the Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF). Newly coined words must respect French phonetics and Latin-character transliteration rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal from the Registraire, the declarant has 30 days from notification to file a revised name declaration or a formal review request under the Act respecting the register of enterprises. The Registrar must decide the review within 45 days. An adverse decision may be appealed to the Tribunal administratif du Québec within 60 days of service. The appeal bundle must include the registrar's refusal letter, the original name search report, the corrected French-language declaration, and any OQLF authorization for tokens requiring approval.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for mail processing and service of process only if it includes a physical street address in Quebec and dedicated office staff available to receive official notices during business hours. Pure mail-forwarding virtual offices are not acceptable for the registered office (siège social) because Revenu Québec and the Registraire des entreprises require an actual establishment address. For the wholesale matcha powder distribution industry, a serviced-office arrangement with a physical reception is accepted as sufficient commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability within the first 24 months, reflecting routine Revenu Québec establishment audits, Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) import verification visits for food products, and FINTRAC/AML on-site inspection protocols for reporting entities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2266; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 10-18; Québec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1 (as applicable to the corporate general partner).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Québec law; no escrow account is required. Contributions may be cash or property (a limited partner may not contribute services), as set out in the limited partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Upon the advice of counsel, it is RESOLVED as follows: (1) The shareholder of the general partner subscribes for the common shares set out in the share subscription list, and the officers are authorized to issue same upon receipt of full consideration. (2) The registered office of the general partner and principal place of business of the limited partnership is established at [address], in the Province of Quebec, and authorized corporate records shall be kept there. (3) [Name] is appointed President and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, each with full power, acting singly, to execute registration declarations, banking account forms, contracts, and any ancillary instrument required to organize and maintain the limited partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name validation and pre-registration due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name-search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Québec enterprise register for the proposed enterprise name; verify French-language prominence, distinctiveness and absence of confusing similarity with existing names and trademarks; obtain consents from individuals whose names appear; confirm the proposed activity (wholesale matcha powder, NAICS 424490 / ISIC 4631) is not misleading.
required_dossiers: Proposed enterprise name (French or bilingual format)
Trade-mark search (if relying on registered marks)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or placed in inquiry, file revised names or submit evidence of distinctiveness and consent; the registry may require a fresh declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of limited partnership agreement and general partner organization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial office / corporate counsel (no government registration at this stage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement among at least one general partner and one limited partner; describe contributions, distributions, management powers and restrictions; have the corporate general partner adopt its first board resolution, subscribe shares and appoint officers; ensure notarial or witnessed signatures as required by the partners' agreement.
required_dossiers: Resolution of corporate general partner's board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency is identified, cure by unanimous consent or an addendum to the limited partnership agreement before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – CLIC online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Déclaration d'immatriculation through the CLIC portal; accurately disclose the enterprise name, establishment and mailing addresses, date of formation, general partner details, aggregate sums contributed or committed by limited partners, and the primary business activity; pay the applicable filing fee and submit electronically or at a service point.
required_dossiers: Certificate or evidence of name validity
Copy of executed limited partnership agreement
Authorization or power of attorney for any signing agent
Proof of identity and address of general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry query within the prescribed period; amend and resubmit the declaration; if refusal persists, request review by the registrar or the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining certificate of registration and Québec enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After acceptance, retrieve the attestation or certificate of registration and the NEQ; review registered details for completeness; if the limited partnership will operate outside Québec or hold extra-provincial registration obligations, obtain the appropriate extra-provincial registration or certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration information is inaccurate, file a declaration of correction or request rectification through the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax account registration, banking and annual governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the NEQ, apply to Revenu Québec for QST registration and to the CRA for GST/HST and a business number if the partnership carries on taxable activities; open a bank account using the attestation and agreement; keep partner ledgers, annual information returns and minutes; file the annual registration declaration with the registry as required under the legal publicity Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account application is queried, provide supporting partnership documents; eligible penalties may be mitigated under the Voluntary Disclosures Program.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure import and wholesale distribution; future food-processing or repackaging operations may be regulated by the Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial manufacturing or physical-operation permit is required for pure import-and-wholesale trading of matcha powder; a federal Safe Food for Canadians Act import licence may nevertheless be required before the first import.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA is required for a trading and distribution enterprise that does not process, produce, or discharge industrial waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable wastewater or VOC discharge thresholds; if packaging or warehousing is established, the Québec Environment Quality Act and municipal by-laws on noise, waste and refrigerant emissions will apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety inspection and certificate for the leased office or warehouse; compliance with the Québec Construction Code and Building Act for structural loads; CNESST occupational health and safety compliance for any employees; no specialized civil-defense clearance is required for this trading occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal GST/HST and income tax administration (portal: CRA Business Registration Online, www.canada.ca); Revenu Quebec (RQ) - Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial tax administration (portal: RQ CLIC, www.revenuquebec.ca); Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - mandatory extra-provincial partnership registration (portal: www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File a declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 60 days of starting activities to obtain the NEQ enterprise number. Step 2: Apply via CRA Business Registration Online (or Form RC1) for the 9-digit Business Number and GST/HST program account; a limited partnership is a deemed registrant person under ETA s. 272.1 despite income-tax transparency. Step 3: Register for QST with Revenu Quebec via CLIC or Form LM-101-V; registration is compulsory where the C$30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded, and a non-resident LP must appoint a representative for service (ETA s. 268). Step 4: File the annual T5013 Partnership Information Return and Quebec RL-15, allocate income to partners, and meet any Part XIII/Part I withholding obligations regarding non-resident partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian LPs are income-tax transparent by default (ITA s. 96) but are separate notional registrants for GST/HST/QST. Material elections: (i) ETA s. 272.1(5) election to treat the partnership or the partners as the taxable person for input tax credit purposes; (ii) drop-shipment zero-rating election for matcha delivered in Canada to a non-resident recipient for export (ETA s. 179); (iii) fiscal-period and late-filing elections (ITA s. 96(13), s. 220(3)); (iv) hybrid-mismatch election and ordering rules under ITA ss. 18.4-18.8. Canada has no US-style check-the-box entity classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Value-Added Goods and Services Tax, Excise Tax Act Part IX) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax); GST is 5%, QST is 9.975% calculated on the GST-inclusive base (effective combined burden about 15.47%), administered under a single CRA-RQ joint filing framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (small-supplier limit; ETA s. 148(1) and QSTA equivalent): worldwide taxable supplies of C$30,000 or less in a calendar quarter or in the four preceding calendar quarters; the matcha wholesale distribution operation will exceed the threshold and must register for both GST/HST and QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None: Canada and Quebec do not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping for B2B supplies. Voluntary PEPPOL e-invoicing under the Pan-Canadian B2B E-Invoicing Framework (2024) is optional, and conventional invoices are not rejected. Invoices must still satisfy ETA ss. 223-224 and QST invoice-content rules (vendor identity, BN, QST registration number, date, description, tax amounts), with six-year record retention.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) organic matcha powder physically exported by the LP as a registrant supplier (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 1; mirroring QST Act rules), (ii) supplies of goods delivered in Canada to a non-resident recipient for export (drop-shipment, ETA s. 179), and (iii) services performed and supplied wholly outside Canada. Goods must be exported as soon as reasonable and generally within 60 days after ownership transfer; contemporaneous shipping, customs, and payment evidence must be retained. Plain matcha sold domestically may separately qualify as zero-rated basic groceries under Schedule VI, Part III.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (G11 / Canadian Automated Export Declaration; mandatory above C$2,000 or for controlled goods)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement
Cargo Control Document / customs carrier entry
Commercial invoice, packing list, and purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign-currency inward payment confirmation matched to the invoice
USMCA/CUSMA Certificate of Origin (recommended for US-destined matcha to obtain preferential US duty treatment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec jointly audit export zero-rating claims; missing documentation triggers reversal of the zero-rating and reassessment of the full 14.975% combined GST/QST plus statutory daily compound interest. Penalties: false-statement penalty of 25% of the improperly claimed refund (ETA s. 285); gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of the tax evaded; the normal 4-year reassessment window extends to 12 years for misrepresentation and is unlimited for fraud. General partners and directors face joint and several liability for unremitted net tax (ETA s. 323; Quebec equivalent), and fraudulent refund schemes may attract criminal prosecution. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the 180-day treasury ceiling is an audit-tested internal control for arm's length settlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential supervisors: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) for Quebec payment services; exchange intervention authority rests with the federal Minister of Finance assisted by the Bank of Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has a fully convertible currency with no exchange-control restrictions on either current or capital account transactions. The Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act impose no prior approval, repatriation, or surrender obligations for CAD or foreign currency. Profit remittance from a Quebec Limited Partnership to non-resident limited partners is not FX-restricted, but may attract Canadian non-resident withholding tax (Income Tax Act Part XIII) on distributions that are taxable Canadian-source income, with treaty rate reductions available; CRS/FATCA reporting and NR4/T5013 schedules are required. Foreign currency accounts may be held freely; the Bank of Canada daily noon exchange rate is the standard conversion benchmark for Canadian-dollar functional-currency accounting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender regime exists in Canada. There is no mandatory conversion ratio and no fixed statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in a foreign-currency account at any Canadian Schedule I bank. Compliance obligations are limited to FINTRAC reporting of cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, the Canada Revenue Agency functional-currency rules, and supporting documentation for the Canada Border Services Agency and the Canadian Organic Regime if product-level claims are advertised.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (CAD) and Operational Account (CAD/USD) with treasury and hedging services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury custody and capital escrow; Medium as an auxiliary collection and payout rail. Offshore digital EMIs (UK/EU electronic money institutions) are not authorized deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act. Quebec's Payment Services Act and the AMF licensing regime require a Quebec payment service provider licence for money-transfer activities. An unlicensed offshore EMI must not hold the LP's permanent operating balances; it may only serve as a supplementary FX/collection conduit, subject to FATF-compliant originators and bank-backed settlement into the Schedule I bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one authorized signatory, normally the General Partner or a designated signing officer of the General Partner, must complete a physical KYC interview at a Canadian bank branch. Fully remote onboarding is rarely granted for a newly registered Quebec LP with non-resident capital providers; video-based identity verification may be used only for transparent low-risk structures at the compliance officer's discretion. Where the General Partner is also a corporate entity, its principal natural-person director must attend or present a notarized power of attorney apostilled under the Hague Convention and attested at a Canadian consulate. Each non-resident limited partner holding 25% or more of the LP must provide notarized identity and address verification; a Quebec legal entity (Registraire des entreprises) excerpt and a Canadian financial institution reference or credit history are typically required to satisfy the bank's enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: the LP is controlled by a non-resident corporate General Partner with multi-layer offshore intermediate entities not appearing in the Quebec enterprise register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated Registraire des entreprises du Quebec Relevé d'entreprise; executed LP agreement; full organizational chart reaching natural-person UBOs; passport and residential proof for each UBO; corporate registry extracts for every intermediate entity; sworn source-of-wealth statement for the capital contribution and prior-year audited financial statements of the material parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an offshore location without a clear commercial rationale or with an atypical routing pattern, triggering sanctions and PEP screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GP resolution authorizing the capital call and the specific wire amount; executed capital contribution schedule referenced to the LP agreement; bank statements of the remitting entity supporting the clean source of funds; purchase orders and master supply contract with the Japanese matcha supplier; Japan-side JAS organic certification and health certificate corroborating the trade pipeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators: invoice discrepancies, mismatch between beneficiary name and supplier's bank account, or settlement to a third-party beneficiary in Japan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial documentation set: pro-forma invoice, commercial invoice, clean-on-board bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, insurance certificate, Japanese certificate of origin, JAS organic matcha certificate; a written matching statement linking each invoice to the corresponding payment order in SWIFT MT103 field 70; any third-party off-take agreement with a chain-of-custody addendum and notification to the supplier's bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction pattern: repeated CAD 10,000+ wires to Japan suppliers in a concentrated period inconsistent with the stated inventory build and sales cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual cash-flow forecast and purchase budget; supplier rolling delivery schedules and warehouse inventory reports; bank statements showing inventory asset capitalization in the LP's books; completed FINTRAC-compliant records demonstrating the trades correspond to documented supply contracts; the LP's periodic manager statements confirming commercial substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions arrive by SWIFT MT103 to the LP's designated operational or escrow account at a Schedule I Canadian bank, or domestically through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) where the remitting partner holds a Canadian account. The remitter name must exactly match the limited partner's KYC records; field 70 must state the capital contribution reference and the LP agreement clause; field 50K/56A/57A must be pre-validated to avoid rejection. For any cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, the receiving bank automatically files an Electronic Funds Transfer Report (eFTR) with FINTRAC; for CAD 100,000 or more, the bank may require a documented source-of-funds declaration, including the remitter's bank statement and the GP's capital call notice. The LP should pre-declare all committed limited partners in its KYC file and maintain a capital subscription ledger to demonstrate the exempt money-laundering purpose of the credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements to Japan flow through SWIFT MT103 as regular customer credit transfers for transactional amounts, with MT202 COV used only for interbank cover legs in USD/JPY. For larger or seasonal bulk shipments, the LP may use irrevocable documentary letters of credit (sight or usance 90-180 days) issued by the Canadian bank on the supplier's confirmed L/C, especially where the Japanese supplier requires conforming presentation: original commercial invoice in duplicate, full set clean-on-board bills of lading, packing list, JAS organic certificate, phytosanitary certificate where applicable, and certificate of origin (Form 160). Direct CAD/JPY or USD/JPY settlement executes through the bank's clearing correspondent in Tokyo. All payments must be matched to the supplier's account as named on the contract; any currency conversion is executed on the bank's displayed rate with a dated MT900 confirmation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/JPY FX forward (tenor 30-365 days) executed as an OTC risk-management contract with a Schedule I bank and designated as a hedge of committed Japanese supplier invoices under the LP's internal treasury mandate.

Deliverable CAD/USD FX forward for hedging US-dollar-denominated transport, insurance, and ancillary distribution costs, or for converting USD capital contributions into CAD without spot-market volatility.

Cross-currency swap (CAD/JPY or CAD/USD) permitted where the LP converts a foreign-currency capital injection into CAD while maintaining a scheduled JPY liability leg matched to supplier payment dates.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF): legally permissible under Canadian rules solely for hedging a counterparty currency with no deliverable CAD forward market; NDFs are not appropriate for CAD/JPY or CAD/USD settlement because both leg currencies are freely convertible and delivery is standard.

FX swap (short-tenor spot-forward combination) used to warehouse an imminent supplier payment in JPY without creating overnight open FX risk; each instrument must be documented under the bank's International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement or Canadian Bankers Association master forward agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) in the Quebec Enterprise Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary date of the enterprise registration with REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration surcharge of CAD 102; registration can be struck off by REQ for prolonged default, causing loss of legal recording benefits and potential denial of limited-partner liability protections.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal income tax information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s. 162(2.1) calculated on a per-partner, per-day basis; continued delinquency beyond six months may attract additional penalties and interest under s. 163.2.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Relevé 501 – Annual Partnership Declaration and Information Return (Quebec taxation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or provide complete information exposes the LP to Quebec late-filing penalties of 5% of unreported amounts plus 1% per full month, plus interest; repeated non-compliance may lead to loss of registration privileges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold is prescribed for limited partnerships under Quebec Civil Code. A statutory independent audit is required only if the LP is a reporting issuer, if a specific provincial regime treats it as a large enterprise, or if the limited partnership agreement or a lender covenant mandates audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS as adopted by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board for publicly accountable LPs; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) or IFRS for non-reporting private LPs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not operate a public UBO registry. The general partner must keep and annually confirm a register setting out each limited partner's name, address, and contribution (Civil Code of Québec art. 2220). The REQ annual declaration must name every general partner and the registered office. Any transfer of a partnership interest requires an immediate register entry and, if the REQ declaration changes, an amended filing with REQ. FINTRAC AML/KYC requirements additionally mandate ongoing beneficial-owner identification for commercial relationships.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (Civil Code of Québec, art. 2220)
General Partner's accounting and tax records supporting the annual declaration
Partnership agreement and all amending instruments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $150 – $400 per year for Quebec registered office/agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by default; voluntary review engagement approximates $2,500 – $6,000; optional full audit approximates $7,500 – $12,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: A Canadian limited partnership is generally fiscally transparent and is not subject to federal or Quebec corporate income tax on allocated partnership income. Tax is imposed at partner level. For an incorporated partner, the federal general corporate rate is 15% and the Quebec general corporate rate is 11.5%, producing a combined general rate of 26.5%. The federal small-business rate is 9% and the Quebec small-business rate is generally 3.2%, subject to eligibility and business-limit rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level corporate tax holiday generally applies to the limited partnership. Eligible corporate partners may access the federal small-business deduction and Quebec small-business deduction. Taxable income is allocated to partners under the partnership agreement and applicable tax law. Organic certification, food-sector status, or matcha trading activity does not independently create a corporate income tax exemption. Federal and Quebec non-capital losses generally carry forward 20 years and back 3 years; net capital losses generally carry forward indefinitely and back 3 years, subject to statutory restrictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Canada Revenue Agency Form T5013, Partnership Information Return, filed electronically through CRA-approved electronic filing channels, including the T5013 Internet File Transfer where applicable. The partnership generally does not file a T1 or T2 income tax return for its own allocated business income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period. Partnership information slips and summaries are generally due within 3 months after the partnership fiscal period-end. A partnership may be required to file where, among other triggers, it has a corporate partner, a non-resident partner, has carried on business in Canada, or satisfies prescribed income, asset, or information-return conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the limited partnership, business number, partnership account, fiscal period, principal Canadian address, Quebec location information, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the partnership's Canadian business number and registered legal name. Identify the Canadian carrying-on-business location and disclose non-resident partners through the prescribed partner information schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify general partners, limited partners, corporate partners, trusts, individuals, and non-resident partners, including ownership or allocation percentages where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat a non-resident limited partner as a Canadian resident. Record residency, tax identification number, ownership, capital, income allocation, and applicable treaty residence documentation accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of goods sold, inventory, expenses, assets, liabilities, capital accounts, and partnership net income or loss for the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian-source and worldwide partnership financial information as required by the form. Maintain books in Canadian dollars or apply the CRA-approved translation methodology consistently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate business income, property income, capital gains, losses, foreign-source amounts, deductions, and other tax attributes among partners according to the agreement and Canadian tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations must have commercial and legal support and cannot be used to improperly shift Canadian-source income. A non-resident partner may have a Canadian filing obligation under section 150 and related provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issue the applicable T5013 information slip to each partner, including allocated income, losses, capital gains, interest, foreign income, and other relevant amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the correct partner residency code and tax identification number. Do not report a distribution as a substitute for the partner's allocated taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where Quebec filing requirements apply, file the Quebec partnership information return, generally Form TP-600-V and related schedules, through Revenu Quebec's prescribed electronic or paper process.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose Quebec-source business activity, Quebec allocations, partner residency, and Quebec identification data. A federal T5013 filing does not automatically satisfy all Quebec information-return requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report GST/HST and QST registration numbers and reconcile taxable supplies, input tax credits, input tax refunds, collected tax, and remittances in separate indirect-tax returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border procurement and distribution may create GST/HST and QST registration, import, place-of-supply, and customs obligations even where the partnership has no corporate income tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013 filing generally attracts the greater of CAD 100 and CAD 25 per day, subject to a stated maximum commonly applying at CAD 2,500. Incorrect or incomplete information may attract additional penalties. Failure to issue information slips, failure to provide partner information, gross negligence, false statements, and repeated non-compliance may produce further assessments, interest, and prosecution. Quebec penalties and interest apply separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T106, Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents of Canada, filed electronically through CRA corporate and partnership filing channels where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within 6 months after the end of the reporting period for a partnership or other non-corporate filer, subject to the specific statutory filing rule applicable to the taxpayer and fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business number, name, fiscal period, address, and filer classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Canadian partnership as the filer and provide the correct CRA account and fiscal-period data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, country of residence, relationship, and tax identification number of each non-arm's-length non-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the legal entity name and foreign tax number exactly as shown in official records. Disclose ownership and control relationships, including indirect relationships.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases, sales, rents, royalties, management fees, interest, insurance, financing, derivatives, and other amounts involving non-arm's-length non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross amounts by transaction category, not merely net settlement amounts. Include transactions involving related procurement companies, distributors, financing entities, and IP owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pricing method, currency, payment terms, transaction terms, and arm's-length support.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the tested party, comparable transactions, functional analysis, adjustment methodology, and reasons for selecting the method.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or failure to provide required information may attract a penalty generally calculated at CAD 25 per day, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts, commonly including a CAD 100 minimum and CAD 2,500 maximum. Transfer-pricing penalties may apply separately where a reassessment results from a significant transfer-pricing adjustment and reasonable-efforts requirements are not met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Quebec Form CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed only by a corporate general partner or corporate partner where that entity is taxable in Canada or Quebec. Filing is through CRA's and Revenu Quebec's prescribed electronic systems.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any balance is generally payable 2 months after year-end, or 3 months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations subject to the statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, reserves, capital cost allowance, and partnership income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner must include its taxable Canadian partnership income and other Canadian-source income under the applicable Canadian filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the corporate partner's allocated share of partnership business income, loss, capital gains, and other tax attributes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the T5013 information slip and partnership agreement, but independently verify the allocation against the partnership books and tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose related corporations, ownership, associated corporations, and relevant non-arm's-length transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign related parties and assess T106, transfer-pricing, thin-capitalization, withholding, and treaty obligations separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine Quebec taxable income, business allocation, Quebec deductions, credits, and provincial tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File where the corporate partner carries on business in Quebec or otherwise has a Quebec filing obligation. Federal filing does not replace the Quebec return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: For a corporation, late filing commonly results in a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% of unpaid tax for each complete month late, generally capped at 12 months. Increased penalties may apply for repeated late filing. Interest accrues on unpaid balances, and Quebec imposes its own penalties and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: A limited partnership distribution is generally not a dividend and is not automatically subject to dividend withholding tax. A Canadian corporation paying a dividend to a non-resident is generally subject to 25% Part XIII withholding tax, reduced under an applicable income tax treaty, commonly to 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on recipient ownership, beneficial ownership, and treaty conditions. A partnership must separately analyze withholding on allocated income and payments to non-resident partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The recipient should establish treaty residence using a current certificate of residence or equivalent tax-residency documentation, demonstrate beneficial ownership where relevant, satisfy limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where applicable, and provide the payer with the information required under Canadian withholding rules. The Canadian payer must determine the correct rate, retain supporting documentation, remit withholding to the CRA by the 15th day of the following month, and file the applicable NR4 information return and slips. Treaty relief is not automatic merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty jurisdiction. Canada does not generally operate a universal pre-clearance certificate system for all treaty-reduced payments; the payer must support its rate determination.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% on taxable royalties and interest paid or credited to non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Under many Canadian treaties, interest is reduced to 10% or 15%, and copyright, literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, or other IP royalties are commonly reduced to 10%; exact rates depend on the treaty, payment characterization, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse provisions. Arm's-length interest may qualify for a domestic exemption in specified circumstances, but related-party interest, participating debt interest, thin-capitalization rules, recharacterization rules, and treaty limitations must be reviewed. Payments for goods are generally not subject to Part XIII withholding solely because the seller is non-resident, but services, management fees, software rights, and embedded royalties require separate analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not provide a universal transaction-value threshold that eliminates the statutory requirement to maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. Form T106 reporting is generally triggered for aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents exceeding CAD 1,000,000, subject to statutory exclusions and filing rules. A Canadian taxpayer must maintain records sufficient to support arm's-length pricing, and CRA may request contemporaneous documentation. Canada generally does not impose a separate mandatory OECD-style Master File filing requirement equivalent to some jurisdictions, although a Master File may be requested or be prudent for multinational groups. Quebec generally relies on the federal transfer-pricing framework.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other method producing the most reliable arm's-length result under Canada's hierarchy and documentation requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone general Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the United Arab Emirates or certain other jurisdictions. Substance remains relevant through the Income Tax Act, the transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty principal-purpose and beneficial-ownership concepts, sham and agency doctrines, partnership allocation rules, debt characterization, and common-law anti-avoidance principles. The partnership should maintain real procurement and distribution functions, commercially justified pricing, inventory and logistics records, decision-making evidence, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, banking records, and documented risk control. A non-resident partner or related supplier lacking substantive functions may face recharacterization, denied deductions, treaty relief denial, or transfer-pricing adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating matcha procurement costs, omitting partnership income, creating false invoices, diverting inventory proceeds, misrepresenting partner allocations, or knowingly submitting false T5013, T2, CO-17, T106, GST/HST, or QST information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, arrears interest, civil penalties, gross-negligence penalties, repeated-failure penalties, and possible criminal prosecution. Tax evasion convictions can result in fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to 5 years under the Income Tax Act; other statutes may impose different sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, general partners, and persons directing the conduct may face prosecution and personal fines or imprisonment. Corporate directors may be assessed personally for certain unremitted source deductions and GST/HST amounts. A limited partner normally retains limited liability only while respecting statutory and contractual limitations and not conducting management activities that cause loss of that protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Partnership Misclassification and Improper Limited Liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal limited partnership without a genuine general partner, allowing limited partners to conduct unrestricted management, disguising a corporation's business as a partnership to avoid tax, or allocating profits contrary to the partnership agreement and commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of intended flow-through treatment, reassessment of partners, interest, penalties, application of the general anti-avoidance rule, and potential loss of statutory limited-liability protection under applicable partnership law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is ordinarily liable for partnership obligations. Directors and officers of a corporate general partner may face statutory personal liability for tax remittances, fraud, and other specific obligations. Limited partners may become exposed if they exceed statutory limits or provide guarantees.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing organic matcha from a related foreign supplier at inflated prices, selling to a related foreign distributor below market value, charging unsupported royalties or management fees, using non-commercial financing, or allocating risk to an entity without operational capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to an arm's-length amount, denial or reduction of deductions, withholding-tax assessments, transfer-pricing penalty where statutory conditions are met, interest, T106 penalties, and potential treaty relief denial.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal exposure where they knowingly participated in false records, tax evasion, fraudulent conveyances, or statutory remittance defaults. Ordinary transfer-pricing reassessment does not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GST/HST, QST, Import, and Customs Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming fictitious input tax credits or input tax refunds, undervaluing imported matcha, misclassifying tariff codes, failing to collect or remit GST/HST or QST, using false certificates, or importing food products without required customs and food-regulatory compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of credits, customs duties, seizure, administrative monetary penalties, interest, civil penalties, and criminal prosecution for fraud or false declarations. Separate Canadian food, labeling, import, and organic-claim enforcement may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for certain unremitted GST/HST, source deductions, and related amounts where statutory director-liability conditions are met. Knowingly false customs or tax declarations may result in personal fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Proceeds of Crime, and Sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, structuring wire transfers, disguising beneficial ownership, processing proceeds of crime, ignoring sanctions indicators, or failing to maintain required records where the business falls within a FINTRAC-regulated activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties, compliance orders, asset restraint or forfeiture, criminal prosecution, substantial fines, and imprisonment under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the Criminal Code, or applicable sanctions legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers, directors, general partners, and beneficial owners may face personal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, asset forfeiture, and director or officer disqualification consequences. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty but may arise from criminal process, bail conditions, or court orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold or remit Part XIII tax on taxable royalties, interest, dividends, management fees, or other applicable payments to non-residents; applying treaty rates without residence or beneficial-ownership evidence; or misclassifying royalty payments as goods purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment against the Canadian payer for unremitted withholding, penalties, arrears interest, NR4 filing penalties, and possible director liability under statutory remittance provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for specified unremitted source deductions and withholding amounts if the statutory conditions are satisfied. Knowingly fraudulent withholding certificates or records may lead to criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring partnership assets to related parties for less than value, paying insiders while taxes are unpaid, stripping inventory proceeds, granting sham security, or continuing to trade while insolvent and incurring liabilities without reasonable prospect of payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction reversal, clawback, preference recovery, oppression or fiduciary claims, bankruptcy proceedings, civil damages, tax collection measures, and possible criminal fraud charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners, directors, officers, and persons who authorized improper transfers may face restitution, contribution claims, civil judgments, and in serious fraud cases criminal fines or imprisonment. A routine commercial insolvency does not itself pierce the corporate veil.
